round1_p01_review_txt: engine/schema identity check added (db_meta.engine=='airag' + exact schema_migrations version match) — open_encrypted no longer trusts a valid key alone
PRAGMA cipher_version asserted non-empty as proof of real SQLCipher, not just 'module imported + SELECT worked'
key length validated before any file/connection is touched
sqlite-vec promoted to a core dependency; uv exact-version pin relaxed to a floor
round2_live_review: found+fixed: journal_mode=WAL mutates on-disk bytes even with no row-data change (measured empirically) — was being applied BEFORE identity/schema verification, violating 'refuse foreign DB without modification'. Now deferred to _enable_wal(), called only after verification succeeds (or on a brand-new DB being created)
found+fixed: schema check used '> SCHEMA_VERSION' which let a missing/lower/None version through — changed to exact '!= SCHEMA_VERSION'

found+fixed: init_db's exists-then-create was a TOCTOU race; original fix (flock-guarded sidecar lock file, deleted after use) had a genuine double-init bug caught live by a 4-thread concurrency test — a deleted-then-recreated lock file let two threads lock *different* inodes under the same path name. Replaced entirely with os.open(path, O_CREAT|O_EXCL) as the sole exclusivity mechanism: atomic, no sidecar file, and as a side effect now also refuses a pre-existing *empty* placeholder file (previously allowed)
changed: a failed init no longer auto-deletes its partial artifact (DB/-wal/-shm) — preserved for human inspection, consistent with 'no destructive delete without a human'
open_encrypted now connects via a `mode=rw` URI so the SQLite driver itself refuses to create a missing file, on top of the earlier app-level exists() check
round3_live_review: found+fixed: the mode=rw URI was hand-built as f"file:{p}?mode=rw" — a path containing ?, #, or % would be misparsed as URI query/fragment/percent-escapes and could open the wrong file. Fixed to Path.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=rw", which percent-encodes the path correctly; verified with a real round-trip test using a path containing spaces, #, %, and ?
round4_live_review: found+fixed: key validation only checked length, not type. init_db(path, 'x'*32) (a 32-char str, not bytes) passed the length check, then os.open(O_EXCL) created the file, and only then did key_bytes.hex() raise AttributeError inside _apply_raw_key — i.e. the file got created before the bad input was rejected. Reproduced live, then fixed: _validate_key_length now checks isinstance(key_bytes, bytes) first (TypeError) before the length check, and both init_db and open_encrypted validate before touching the filesystem/connecting. Regression tests added for both entry points confirming no file is created.
round5_owner_independent_rerun: owner independently re-ran the full 46/46 suite and confirmed it, then cross-checked evidence claims against actual test code and found two gaps: fixed both, see below

found+fixed: test_extension_loading_disabled_even_on_failure did not call vecext.try_load_vec0 at all — it re-implemented the enable/disable sequence inline in the test itself, so a real bug in try_load_vec0's failure path would not have been caught. Rewritten to monkeypatch sqlite_vec.load to raise, call the real try_load_vec0(con), and assert both its return value (False) and that extension loading is disabled afterward on that same live connection

added: test_fts5_and_vec0_rollback_together_in_one_transaction — previously only FTS5 rollback was tested in isolation; this exercises FTS5 + vec0 inserts inside one BEGIN, rolled back together, both absent afterward
corrected: this evidence file's blanket 'every test opens a real SQLCipher connection' claim was imprecise — see test_suite.result below for the accurate breakdown

test_suite.result: 47 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. No test uses unittest.mock/fake objects standing in for the DB driver. Breakdown by connection type: the large majority open a real SQLCipher connection via sqlcipher3 against a temp file or :memory:; a deliberate minority open a real stdlib sqlite3 (non-SQLCipher) connection — this is intentional, not a mock, in exactly two places: (1) creating a genuine plaintext SQLite fixture file to prove the encrypted-open path refuses it, and (2) proving a genuine stdlib sqlite3.connect() cannot read an already-encrypted file. test_vecext.py's monkeypatch (round5) patches sqlite_vec.load to inject a failure, and still calls the real vecext.try_load_vec0 against a real sqlite3 connection — the DB layer itself is never mocked, only the third-party extension's load() is made to fail on purpose. Includes real 4-thread and 2-thread concurrency races against the actual O_EXCL init path.
